name: TUM RS-VIO (TUM Rolling-Shutter Visual-Inertial Odometry dataset)
sensor: 2x IDS uEye UI-3241LE-M-GL, 1280x1024 grayscale 16-bit, 20 Hz; Bosch BMI160 IMU 200 Hz
shutter: cam0/left = GS; cam1/right = RS (same sensor model, mode switched)
readout_ms: 30.18 (1024 rows x 29.4737 us row time; row time from dataset page)
scan_direction: row-wise (paper: only image y matters for capture time); top-to-bottom not stated
gt_poses: YES - OptiTrack Flex13 mocap 120 Hz, median-filtered, time-aligned to gyro, expressed in IMU frame
gs_twin: YES - hardware-synced GS stereo partner (different viewpoint; stereo baseline)
size: 10 seqs, ~7 min, 475 m total; EuRoC tars 1.1-3.6 GB each (~19.9 GB total); calibrated bags ~46.3 GB total
download: direct public HTTP (https://cdn3.vision.in.tum.de/rolling/), bag or EuRoC/DSO tar
needs_human: NO (but license unstated - confirm before redistribution)
timestamp_convention: Page (verbatim): 'Note that for the calibration sequences, both cameras were operating in global-shutter mode. This means the timestamps for the rolling-shutter images refer to the first row. In general, timestamps denote the middle of the exposure interval.' -> RS stamp = first row (mid-exposure); wording ambiguous
notes: Best real RS+GS twin with mocap. Already used in EXP0/EXP1. Ten sequences, mean speed 0.7-1.4 m/s (paper Tab. I).

name: ADVIO
sensor: Apple iPhone 6s back camera, 1280x720 portrait, 60 fps (ARKit-controlled, H.264); also Google Pixel (ARCore poses) and Tango (fisheye ~5 fps)
gt_poses: YES - pure INS on iPhone IMU + manual position fixes from floor plans/reference video (not mocap); 100 Hz
indoor_outdoor: both (mall, metro station, offices, urban/suburban outdoor)
size: 23 sequences, ~4.5 km, ~5.1 GB uncompressed (71-255 MB per zip)
download: direct public (Zenodo record 1476931; wget loop in README)
timestamp_convention: all sensors synced; iPhone stamps converted to 'time interval since device boot'; exposure reference point not stated
notes: GT is INS+manual fixes, so pose accuracy is far coarser than mocap; poor for RS-induced error at mm/deg level. Good as in-the-wild phone RS stress test only.

shutter: RS rendered line-by-line + time-synced GS twin
readout_ms: 33.33 (480 rows x 69.44 us; paper Sec. III-C)
gs_twin: YES (GS frame with same start time)
size: 2 trajectories x 3 speeds (slow/medium/fast) = 6 sequences; size unknown
license: CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (data, per paper); paper itself CC BY 4.0
download: official URL http://aric.whu.edu.cn/rsvi-dataset.html returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-29
timestamp_convention: 'Each frame of an RS image has a corresponding GS image with the same starting time' -> RS stamp = first-row start
notes: Not real data. Useful only as a sanity check for RS synthesis; superseded by our own renders.

name: PennCOSYVIO
sensor: 3x GoPro Hero 4 Black, Skybotix VI-Sensor (2x 752x480 gray 20 fps), 2x Google Tango (bottom 1920x1080 RGB 30 fps, top 640x480 gray 30 fps)
shutter: RS: 3 GoPros + Tango-bottom RGB; GS: VI-Sensor + Tango-top
gs_twin: PARTIAL (GS cameras on same rig, different viewpoints)
size: ~150 m path walked several times (per ADVIO paper); sequence count/size not stated
notes: ~10 cm GT is too coarse to measure RS-induced pose error. Lower priority.

name: Aria Digital Twin (ADT)
sensor: Project Aria glasses: 1 RGB (1408x1408 in ADT per paper), 2 mono SLAM cams, 2 IMUs; 30 fps
shutter: RGB = RS; SLAM cameras = GS ('specified as global shutter sensors')
readout_ms: 5 ms for 1408x1408 binned/cropped mode; 16.26 ms at full 2880x2880 (Aria docs)
scan_direction: row-wise along sensor rows (Aria formula uses row(p) along the dimension aligned with sensor rows); orientation vs. stored image must be checked
gt_poses: YES - OptiTrack mocap, Aria-Optitrack timecode sync <10 us average
gt_depth: YES - per-frame depth rendered from digital twin (mm, camera Z)
gt_3d: YES - digitized scene + object models (.glb), object 6DoF poses
gs_twin: PARTIAL (GS mono SLAM cams on same device; not pixel-aligned)
size: 200 sequences (~400 min) per paper/projectaria.com; docs page says 236 sequences (inconsistent); GB unknown
license: ADT dataset license agreement (projectaria.com; text not read)
download: projectaria.com form: submit email + agree to license, then aria_dataset_downloader
timestamp_convention: RGB per-pixel t(p) = t_image + (row(p)/H - 0.5) * readout -> image stamp = centre-of-exposure of middle row; SLAM cams stamp = centre of exposure
verified: YES (whether GT depth is rendered RS-aware is UNVERIFIED)
notes: Only real dataset found with documented RS readout + mocap poses + dense GT depth + meshes. Short 5 ms readout -> small RS effect except fast head turns.

name: Waymo Open Dataset - Perception
sensor: 5 cameras (F/FL/FR 1920x1280, SL/SR 1920x1040 after crop+downsample) + 5 LiDARs
shutter: RS ('The camera images are captured with rolling shutter scanning, where the exact scanning mode can vary from scene to scene')
readout_ms: per image: camera_readout_done_time - camera_trigger_time - shutter (devkit camera_model.cc); value not inspected (data behind login)
scan_direction: per camera in CameraCalibration.rolling_shutter_direction enum {UNKNOWN, TOP_TO_BOTTOM, LEFT_TO_RIGHT, BOTTOM_TO_TOP, RIGHT_TO_LEFT, GLOBAL_SHUTTER}
gt_poses: YES - per-image SDC (vehicle) pose + velocity (v_x,v_y,v_z,w_x,w_y,w_z in global frame) at pose_timestamp; camera extrinsic in calibration
gt_depth: via LiDAR projection (devkit has RS-aware projection)
size: 1150 scenes x 20 s (CVPR'20 paper); later versions and GB UNVERIFIED (behind login)
license: Waymo Dataset License Agreement for Non-Commercial Use (March 2025); devkit Apache-2.0; camera model code under src/waymo_open_dataset/wdl_limited/ with its own LICENSE
download: Google sign-in + accept license (waymo.com/open/data/perception redirects to Google OAuth)
timestamp_convention: proto comment: desired timestamp per column = middle of exposure of that column; 'time image center (= middle of exposure of middle row)'. Devkit: t(row) = camera_trigger_time + 0.5*shutter + readout*row/H (TOP_TO_BOTTOM). pose given at pose_timestamp
verified: YES (proto + devkit source + paper); per-image readout values UNVERIFIED
notes: Best-documented RS timing of any real dataset. Fields: CameraImage.pose(3), velocity(4), pose_timestamp(5), shutter(6), camera_trigger_time(7), camera_readout_done_time(8); CameraCalibration.rolling_shutter_direction(6). Paper: column-by-column scan in proto example (left->right). Sync error bounded [-6ms,7ms] @99.7%.

name: ScanNet++ (iPhone stream; v2)
sensor: iPhone 13 Pro RGB 1920x1440 @60 FPS + LiDAR depth 256x192 @60 FPS; Sony Alpha 7 IV DSLR fisheye (static); Faro Focus Premium laser scanner
shutter: iPhone: RS presumed, NOT documented; DSLR: static shots (shutter irrelevant)
gt_poses: YES (pseudo-GT): COLMAP registration of iPhone frames to laser-scan renders + dense photometric refinement; frames with >0.3 m depth disagreement filtered; ARKit poses also provided
gt_depth: YES - render mesh depth for iPhone frames (toolkit common.render); also iPhone LiDAR depth
gt_3d: YES - sub-mm laser scans, Poisson meshes
size: 1006 scenes (docs); default download ~1.5 TB; meshes+semantics 132 GB; point clouds 720 GB
download: create account, login, submit application -> token
verified: YES (no RS timing exists in docs)
notes: Strong 3D GT but RS readout must be estimated (e.g., fit per-device line delay). Per-frame pseudo-GT pose is a single pose per frame, so RS will bias it. MapAnything trains/tests on ScanNet++ v2.
